problem.reason: Articulation between mechanically/topologically separate regions may legitimately reveal new negative space. Background area alone carries no continuity authority.

shipping_contract.shared_edge_definition: An undirected canonical mesh edge referenced by two or more faces through the same canonical vertex indices.
shipping_contract.per_frame_view_proof: Every incident face copy of each shared edge must carry bit-exact equal projected XY endpoints from the single posed canonical vertex matrix.
shipping_contract.raster_control: Two triangles exactly tiling a square must leave zero uncovered pixel centers along their interior shared diagonal.
shipping_contract.native_reference_relation: Stage45 already requires native/reference owner and RGBA parity, so a native raster divergence cannot bypass the canonical continuity proof.

adversarial_controls.true_seam_crack: Two faces retain shared canonical edge indices while one face consumes a 0.25 px shifted projected copy of an endpoint; continuity proof must fail.
adversarial_controls.legitimate_negative_space: Two topologically separate triangles/components move far apart; no shared-edge continuity authority exists and the gap must not fail.
adversarial_controls.raster_shared_edge: Exact two-triangle square under product HALF_INTEGER_TOP_LEFT rasterizer has full 16x16 coverage with no diagonal crack.

claim_boundary: This closes same-canonical-mesh interior seam continuity only. It deliberately does not assert that gaps between mechanically separate components are cracks, and does not invent underlay or non-detachability semantics.
